# Ships, cargo and naval orders

**Historical study:** [Black Sea shipping and disposal](../docs/historical-studies/black-sea-network.md).

## Cargo, loading and release

Messages about Nikolaev, Poti and Batum describe cargo on hand, loading opportunities and inquiries about releasing supplies. Tobacco ready for loading and an inquiry about oil establish availability or a requested decision, without establishing that either consignment departed.

| Subject | Summary | Page editions |
|---|---|---|
| **Nikolaev supply cargo and shipping decisions** | A report describes steamers entering Nikolaev and goods remaining aboard under military guard, and asks how the recipient intends to proceed. | [p. 199](../cases/pages/199.md#source-p199-a1) |
| **Tobacco awaiting loading at Poti** | Tobacco is reported ready at Poti; the sender asks when loading will be possible. No vessel departure is reported. | [p. 113](../cases/pages/113.md#source-p113-c) |
| **An inquiry about releasing oil** | The sender asks whether Izzet Pasha’s renewed order to release oil has succeeded. The result of that order is not supplied. | [p. 83](../cases/pages/083.md#source-p83-a) |

## Ship sales, payment and authority

The proposed Corcovado terms allocate seizure and nonpayment risks. Other Turkish purchase proposals require immediate payment and authorization; naval armistice instructions provide a separate record of command requirements.

| Subject | Summary | Page editions |
|---|---|---|
| **Corcovado sale terms, payment and transfer of title** | Proposed terms allocate seizure and nonpayment risks and restrict resale. A separate report describes Turkish crewing; a later order halts an unsettled sale or outstanding transfer of title and gives cash payment in Germany as the condition to state to Turkey. | [p. 165](../cases/pages/165.md#source-p165-a1) · [p. 173](../cases/pages/173.md#source-p173-a1) · [p. 200](../cases/pages/200.md#source-p200-b1) |
| **Turkish tonnage purchases and authorization** | The Marineamt discourages sales except in extreme necessity, requires authorization and immediate payment, and questions whether Turkish buyers intend to transport Germans. | [p. 177](../cases/pages/177.md#source-p177-b1) |
| **Naval armistice instructions** | The order directs immediate forwarding, cessation of hostilities at noon on 11 November and assembly of naval forces at their bases. | [p. 178](../cases/pages/178.md#source-p178-a1) |
